G0001.strongs: the first letter of the alphabet; figuratively, only (from its use as a numeral) the first:
senses: Α, α, ἄλφα (which see), τό, indecl., alpha, the first letter of the Greek alphabet. As a numeral, ά = 1, α = 1000. As a prefix, it appears to have at least two and perhaps three distinct senses:
ἀ- (before a vowel, ἀν-) negative, as in ἄ-γνωστος, ἄ-δικος.
ἀ-, ἁ- copulative, indicating community and fellowship, as in ἁ-πλοῦς, ἀ-κολουθέω, ἀ-δελφός.
An intensive force (LS, s. α), as in ἀ-τενίζω is sometimes assumed (but see Boisacq, see word). (AS)

G0003.forms: Ἀβαδδών (Heb. אֲבַדּוֹן, destruction; LXX, ἀπώλεια, only in Wisdom Lit., of the place of the ruined dead: [[r:JOB.26.6|Job 26:6, 28:22, 31:12]], [[r:PSA.88.12|Psa 88:12]], [[r:PRO.15.11|Pro 15:11]]*), indecl.
senses: in NT, Abaddon, the angel of the Abyss: [[r:REV.9.11|Rev 9:11.]]† (AS)

Ἀββά (T, -ᾶ), indecl. (Aram, אַבָּא, emphatic form of אַב = Heb. אָב, father), used in the phrase Ἀ. ὁ παήρ, Abba, Father (see Swete on Mk, I.with): [[r:MRK.14.36|Mrk 14:36]], [[r:ROM.8.15|Rom 8:15]], [[r:GAL.4.6|Gal 4:6]].† (AS)

G0007.forms: Ἀβιά (Heb. אֲבִיָּה, אֲבִיָּהוּ), ὁ, indecl. (in FlJ, Ἀβίας, -α)
G0007.strongs: Abijah, the name of two Israelites
senses: A priest of the line of Eleazar ([[r:1CH.24.3|1Ch 24:3, 10]]): [[r:LUK.1.5|Luk 1:5]]. † (AS)
Ἀβειληνή (T, Rec. Ἀβι-), -ῆς, ἡ, (sc. χώρα), Abilene, a district in the Anti-Lebanon: [[r:LUK.3.1|Luk 3:1.]]† (AS)

G0011.forms: Ἀβραάμ (Heb. אַבְרָהָם), ὁ, indecl. (in FlJ, Ἄβραμος, -ου; MM, VGT, see word)

G0012.root: from [[w:G0001]] (as a negative particle) and a variation of [[w:G1037]]
senses: in cl., boundless, bottomless (e.g. ἄ. πέλαγος, ἄ. πλοῦτος Æsch.).
NT, as subst. (MM, VGT, see word), ἡ ἄ. (sc. χώρα), the abyss;

of the underworld, as the abode of the dead: [[r:ROM.10.7|Rom 10:7]] (a paraphrase of [[r:DEU.30.13|Deu 30:13]] LXX); as the abode of demons, [[r:LUK.8.31|Luk 8:31]], [[r:REV.9.1|Rev 9:1, 2, 11, 11:7, 17:8, 20:1, 3]] (Cremer, 2). † (AS)
to do good, show kindness: [[r:1TI.6.18|1 Ti 6:18]] (Cremer, 8).† ἀγαθουργέω, -ῶ, contracted form (rare, see WH, App., 145) of ἀγαθοερ- (which see), to do good: [[r:ACT.14.17|Act 14:17.]]† (AS)

G0015.strongs: to be a well-doer (as a favor or a duty)
senses: ἀγαθὀ-ποιέω, -ῶ (= cl. ἀγαθὸν ποιεῖν, εὐεργετεῖν), to do good;
for another's benefit: [[r:MRK.3.4|Mrk 3:4]] (T, ἀγαθὸν ποιῆσαι), [[r:LUK.6.9|Luk 6:9]]; (with) accusative of person(s), [[r:LUK.6.33|Luk 6:33, 35]] (Cremer, 8). † (AS)
doing well, acting rightly (Plut.): [[r:1PE.2.14|1Pe 2:14]] (Cremer, 8; MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)

in general, good, in physical and in moral sense, used of persons, things, acts, conditions, etc., applied to that which is regarded as "perfect in its kind, so as to produce pleasure and satisfaction,... that which, in itself good, is also at once for the good and the advantage of him who comes in contact with it" (Cremer, 3): γῆ, [[r:LUK.8.8|Luk 8:8]]; δένδρον, [[r:MAT.7.18|Mat 7:18]]; καρδία, [[r:LUK.8.15|Luk 8:15]]; δόσις, [[r:JAS.1.17|Jas 1:17]]; μέρις, [[r:LUK.10.42|Luk 10:42]]; ἔργον (frequently in Pl.), [[r:PHP.1.6|Php 1:6]]; ἐλπίς, [[r:2TH.2.16|2Th 2:16]]; θησαυρός, [[r:MAT.12.35|Mat 12:35]]; μνεία, [[r:1TH.3.6|1Th 3:6]] (cf. [[r:2MA.7.20|2Ma 7:20]]); as subst., τὸ ἀ, that which is morally good, beneficial, acceptable to God, [[r:ROM.12.2|Rom 12:2]]; ἐργάζεσθαι τὸ ἀ, [[r:ROM.2.10|Rom 2:10]], [[r:EPH.4.28|Eph 4:28]]; πράσσειν, [[r:ROM.9.11|Rom 9:11]], [[r:2CO.5.10|2Co 5:10]]; διώκειν, [[r:1TH.5.15|1Th 5:15]]; μιμεῖσθαι, III Jo 11; κολλᾶσθαι τῷ ἀ, [[r:ROM.12.9|Rom 12:9]]; ερωτᾶν περὶ τοῦ ἀ., [[r:MAT.19.17|Mat 19:17]]; διάκονος εἰς τὸ ἀ., [[r:ROM.13.4|Rom 13:4]]; τὸ ἀ. σου, thy favour, benefit, Phm 14; pl., τὰ ἀ., of goods, possessions, [[r:LUK.12.18|Luk 12:18]]; of spiritual benefits, [[r:ROM.10.15|Rom 10:15]], [[r:HEB.9.11|Heb 9:11, 10:1]]. ἀ is opposite to πονηρός, [[r:MAT.5.45|Mat 5:45, 20:5]]; κακός, [[r:ROM.7.19|Rom 7:19]]; φαῦλος, [[r:ROM.9.11|Rom 9:11]], [[r:2CO.5.10|2Co 5:10]] (cf. MM, VGT, see word). SYN.: καλός, δίκαιος. κ. properly refers to goodliness as manifested in form: ἀ. to inner excellence (cf. the cl. καλὸς κἀγαθός and ἐν καρδία κ. καὶ ἀ., [[r:LUK.8.15|Luk 8:15]]). In [[r:ROM.5.7|Rom 5:7]], where it is contrasted with δ., ἀ. implies a kindliness and attractiveness not necessarily possessed by the δίκαιος, who merely measures up to a high standard of rectitude (cf. ἀγαθωσύνη). (AS)

G0019.forms: ἀγαθωσύνη (on the termination, see: ἁγιότης, and cf. WH, App., 152; MM, VGT, see word), -ης, ἡ
senses: (ἀγαθός), goodness (representing "the kindlier, as δικαιοσύνη, the sterner element in the ideal character," AE, Eph., 5:9; on its relation to χρηστότης, see Tr., Syn., §lxiii): [[r:ROM.15.14|Rom 15:14]], [[r:GAL.5.22|Gal 5:22]], [[r:2TH.1.11|2Th 1:11]].† (AS)
(ἀγαλλιάω), exultation, exuberant joy: [[r:LUK.1.44|Luk 1:44]], [[r:ACT.2.46|Act 2:46]], [[r:HEB.1.9|Heb 1:9]], Ju 24; χαρὰ καὶ ἀ., [[r:LUK.1.14|Luk 1:14]] (Cremer, 592).† (AS)

G0021.forms: ἀγαλλιάω, -ῶ, Hellenistic form of cl. ἀγάλλω, to glorify, mid. -ομαι, to exult in
G0021.strongs: properly, to jump for joy, i.e. exult
G0021.kjv: be (exceeding) glad, with exceeding joy, rejoice (greatly)
senses: to exult, rejoice greatly: before ἐπί, with dative, [[r:LUK.1.47|Luk 1:47]]; with dative mod., [[r:1PE.1.8|1Pe 1:8]], [[r:REV.19.7|Rev 19:7]]. Mid., with same sense: [[r:MAT.5.12|Mat 5:12]], [[r:LUK.10.21|Luk 10:21]], [[r:ACT.2.26|Act 2:26, 16:34]], [[r:1PE.4.13|1Pe 4:13]]; before ἵνα, [[r:JHN.8.56|Jhn 8:56]]; ἐν, [[r:JHN.5.35|Jhn 5:35]] (1 aor. pass. perh. as mid.; but see Mozley, Psalter, 5), [[r:1PE.1.6|1Pe 1:6]] (Cremer, 590).† (AS)

G0023.strongs: akin to the base of); to be greatly afflicted, i.e. (figuratively) indignant
G0023.kjv: be much (sore) displeased, have (be moved with, with) indignation
senses: to be indignant: [[r:MAT.21.15|Mat 21:15, 26:8]], [[r:MRK.10.14|Mrk 10:14, 14:4]]; before περί, [[r:MAT.20.24|Mat 20:24]], [[r:MRK.10.41|Mrk 10:41]]; before ὅτι, [[r:LUK.13.14|Luk 13:14]] (see MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)

G0025.strongs: to love (in a social or moral sense)
senses: to love, to feel and exhibit esteem and goodwill to a person, to prize and delight in a thing.

Of human affection, to men: τ. πλησίον, [[r:MAT.5.43|Mat 5:43]]; τ. ἐχθρούς, ib. 44; to Christ, [[r:JHN.8.42|Jhn 8:42]]; to God, [[r:MAT.22.37|Mat 22:37]]; with accusative of thing(s), [[r:LUK.11.43|Luk 11:43]], [[r:JHN.12.43|Jhn 12:43]], [[r:EPH.5.25|Eph 5:25]], II [[r:TIM.4.8|Tim 4:8]], 10, [[r:HEB.1.9|Heb 1:9]], [[r:1PE.2.17|1Pe 2:17, 3:10]], [[r:2PE.2.15|2Pe 2:15]], [[r:1JN.2.15|1Jn 2:15]], [[r:REV.12.11|Rev 12:11]].

Christ's love: to men, [[r:MRK.10.21|Mrk 10:21]]; to God, [[r:JHN.14.31|Jhn 14:31]]; with cogn. accusative, [[r:JHN.17.26|Jhn 17:26]], [[r:EPH.2.4|Eph 2:4]]. SYN.: φιλέω. From its supposed etymology (Thayer, LS; but see also Boisacq) ἀ. is commonly understood properly to denote love based on esteem (diligo), as distinct from that expressed by φιλέω (amo), spontaneous natural affection, emotional and unreasoning. If this distinction holds, ἀ. is fitly used in NT of Christian love to God and man, the spiritual affection which follows the direction of the will, and which, therefore, unlike that feeling which is instinctive and unreasoned, can be commanded as a duty. (Cf. ἀγάπη, and v. Tr., Syn. §xii; Cremer, 9, 592; and esp. MM, VGT, see word) (AS)

G0026.strongs: love, i.e. affection or benevolence; specially (plural) a love-feast
senses: love, goodwill, esteem. Outside of bibl. and eccl. books, there is no clear instance (with Deiss., LAE, 18:4, 70:2, cf. the same writer in Constr. Quar., ii, 4; and with MM, VGT, see word, cf. Dr. Moulton in Exp. Times, xxvi, 3, 139). In NT, like ἀγαπάω, -ῶ,

In pl., love feasts: Ju 12 (DB, iii, 157). SYN.: φιλία. ἀ., signifying properly (see: ἀγαπάω) love which chooses its object, is taken over from LXX, where its connotation is more general, into NT, and there used exclusively to express that spiritual bond of love between God and man and between man and man, in Christ, which is characteristic of Christianity. It is thusdistinct from φιλία, friendship ([[r:JAS.4.4|Jas 4:4]] only), στοργή, natural affection (in NT only in compounds, see: ἄστοργος) and ἔρως, sexual love, which is not used in NT, its place being taken by ἐπιθυμία. (Cf. ἀγαπάω; and see Abbott, Essays, 70f.; DB, vol. i., 555; Cremer, 13, 593; MM, VGT, see word). (AS)

by Christians, of one another: [[r:1CO.4.14|1Co 4:14]]; frequently as form of address, [[r:1CO.10.14|ib 10:14]]; opposite to ἐχθρός, [[r:ROM.11.28|Rom 11:28]] (see AR, Eph., 229; Cremer, 17; MM, VGT, see word). (AS)
Ἅγαρ (Rec. Ἄ-), ἡ, indecl. (in FlJ, Ἀγάρα, -ης, Heb. הָגָר), Hagar (Gen.16): [[r:GAL.4.24|Gal 4:24,25]].† (AS)

G0029.forms: ἀγγαρεύω (from the Persian; cf. Vg. angiare, and the Heb. אִגֶרֶת; on the orthogr., see Bl., §6, 1; M, Pr., 46)
G0029.strongs: properly, to be a courier, i.e. (by implication) to press into public service
senses: to impress into public service, employ a courier; hence, to compel to perform a service (prob. common in the vernac.; cf. Deiss., BS, 86f., MM, Exp., iv; VGT, see word): [[r:MAT.5.41|Mat 5:41, 27:32]], [[r:MRK.15.21|Mrk 15:21]].† (AS)

G0030.root: from ἄγγος (a pail, perhaps as bent
G0030.strongs: compare the base of); a receptacle

G0032.strongs: compare) (to bring tidings); a messenger; especially an "angel"; by implication, a pastor
senses: As in LXX, in the special sense of angel, a spiritual, heavenly being, attendant upon God and employed as his messenger to men, to make known his purposes, as [[r:LUK.1.11|Luk 1:11]], or to execute them, as [[r:MAT.4.6|Mat 4:6.]] The ἄ. in [[r:REV.1.20|Rev 1:20-2:1]], al., is variously understood as (1) a messenger or delegate, (2) a bishop or ruler, (3) a guardian angel, (4) the prevailing spirit of each church, i.e. the Church itself. (Cf. Swete, Ap)., in l.; DB, iv, 991; Thayer, see word; Cremer, 18; MM, VGT, see word) (AS)
(γενεαλογέω), without genealogy, i.e. without recorded pedigree (cf. [[r:NEH.7.64|Neh 7:64]]): [[r:HEB.7.3|Heb 7:3]] (Cremer, 152; MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)

G0036.strongs: properly, without kin, i.e. (of unknown descent, and by implication) ignoble
senses: of no family, ignoble, base (opposite to ἀγαθός, Soph., Fr., 105): opposite to εὐγενής, [[r:1CO.1.28|1Co 1:28]] (for exx. from π., see MM, VGT, see word). † (AS)

G0037.strongs: to make holy, i.e. (ceremonially) purify or consecrate; (mentally) to venerate
senses: to dedicate, separate, set apart for God; of things: [[r:MAT.23.17|Mat 23:17,19]], [[r:2TI.2.21|2Ti 2:21]]; of persons: Christ, [[r:JHN.10.36|Jhn 10:36, 17:19]].

to purify, make conformable in character to such dedication: forensically, to free from guilt, [[r:1CO.6.11|1Co 6:11]], [[r:EPH.5.26|Eph 5:26]], [[r:HEB.2.11|Heb 2:11, 10:10, 14, 29, 13:12]]; internally, by actual sanctification of life, [[r:JHN.17.17|Jhn 17:17, 19]], [[r:ACT.20.32|Act 20:32, 26:18]], [[r:ROM.15.16|Rom 15:16]], [[r:1CO.1.2|1Co 1:2, 7:14]], [[r:1TH.5.23|1Th 5:23]], [[r:REV.22.11|Rev 22:11]]; of a nonbeliever influenced by marriage with a Christian, [[r:1CO.7.14|1Co 7:14.]]
In the intermediate sense of ceremonial or levitical purification:
to treat as holy: [[r:MAT.6.9|Mat 6:9]], [[r:LUK.11.2|Luk 11:2]], [[r:1PE.3.16|1Pe 3:16]] (Cremer, 53, 602; MM, VGT, see word). † (AS)

G0038.strongs: properly, purification, i.e. (the state) purity; concretely (by Hebraism) a purifier
senses: (ἁγιάζω), as an active verbal noun in -μός, it signifies properly the process τὸ ἁγιάζειν, rather than the resultant state, ἁγιωσύνη, hence,

sanctification: so strictly in [[r:ROM.6.19|Rom 6:19,22]] (but see Meyer), [[r:1CO.1.30|1Co 1:30]], [[r:1TH.4.3|1Th 4:3]],7, [[r:2TH.2.13|2Th 2:13]], [[r:HEB.12.14|Heb 12:14]], [[r:1PE.1.2|1Pe 1:2]]. Elsewhere it perhaps (Ellic.; but see Milligan, Th., 48) inclines to the resultant state: [[r:1TH.4.4|1Th 4:4]], [[r:1TI.2.15|1Ti 2:15]] (Cremer, 55, 602). † (AS)

G0040.strongs: sacred (physically, pure, morally blameless or religious, ceremonially, consecrated)
senses: (τό ἅγός, religious awe; ἅζω, to venerate), primarily, dedicated to the gods, sacred (Hdt.; rare in Att., never in Hom., Hes. and Trag., who use ἁγνός), hence, holy, characteristic of God, separated to God, worthy of veneration.
Its highest application is to God himself, in his purity, majesty, and glory: [[r:LUK.1.49|Luk 1:49]], [[r:JHN.17.11|Jhn 17:11]], [[r:REV.4.8|Rev 4:8]]. Hence
of things and places which have a claim to reverence as sacred to God, e.g. the Temple: [[r:MAT.24.15|Mat 24:15]], [[r:HEB.9.1|Heb 9:1]];
of persons employed by him, as angels: [[r:1TH.3.13|1Th 3:13]]; prophets, [[r:LUK.1.70|Luk 1:70]]; apostles, [[r:EPH.3.5|Eph 3:5.]]
Applied to persons as separated to God's service:
In the moral sense of sharing God's purity: [[r:MRK.6.20|Mrk 6:20]], [[r:JHN.17.11|Jhn 17:11]], [[r:ACT.3.14|Act 3:14]], [[r:REV.3.7|Rev 3:7]].

Of pure, clean sacrifices and offerings: [[r:1CO.7.14|1Co 7:14]], [[r:EPH.1.4|Eph 1:4]]. SYN.: ἁγνός, pure, both in ceremonial and spiritual sense; ἱερός (sacer), sacred, that which is inviolable because of its (external) relation to God; ὅσιος (sanctus as opposite to nefas), that which is based on everlasting ordinances of right. (Cf. Tr., Syn., §lxxxviii; DB, ii, 399 f.; Cremer, 34, 594-601; MM, VGT, see word) (AS)
(ἅγιος), sanctity, holiness, regarded, properly, as an abstract quality (see next word, and cf. Lft. Notes, 49; MM, VGT, see word): [[r:2CO.1.12|2Co 1:12]], [[r:HEB.12.10|Heb 12:10]].† (AS)
(ἅγιος), holiness, the state in man resulting from ἁγιασμός, which see: [[r:ROM.1.4|Rom 1:4]], [[r:2CO.7.1|2Co 7:1]], [[r:1TH.3.13|1Th 3:13]] (Cremer, 52; MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)

G0046.forms: ἄγναφος, -ον (= ἄγναπτος, γνάπτω, late form of κνάπτω, to card wool)
G0046.root: from [[w:G0001]] (as a negative particle) and the same as [[w:G1102]]

senses: purity: [[r:1TI.4.12|1Ti 4:12, 5:2]] (Cremer, 58. For exx. of ceremonial use in π., see MM, Exp., iv).† (AS)

G0048.strongs: to make clean, i.e. (figuratively) sanctify (ceremonially or morally)

G0050.strongs: not to know (through lack of information or intelligence); by implication, to ignore (through disinclination)
G0050.kjv: (be) ignorant(-ly), not know, not understand, unknown
senses: to be ignorant, not to know: absol., Ι [[r:TIT.1.13|Ti 1:13]], [[r:HEB.5.2|Heb 5:2]]; with accusative, [[r:ACT.13.27|Act 13:27 17:23]], [[r:ROM.10.3|Rom 10:3]], [[r:2CO.2.11|2Co 2:11]]; ἐν οἷς, [[r:2PE.2.12|2Pe 2:12]]; before ὅτι, [[r:ROM.2.4|Rom 2:4 6:3 7:1]], [[r:1CO.14.38|1Co 14:38]]; οὐ θέλω ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν, a Pauline phrase: with accusative, [[r:ROM.11.25|Rom 11:25]]; before ὑπέρ, [[r:2CO.1.8|2Co 1:8]]; περί, [[r:1CO.12.1|1Co 12:1]], [[r:1TH.4.13|1Th 4:13]]. ὅτι, [[r:ROM.1.13|Rom 1:13]], [[r:1CO.10.1|1Co 10:1]] (for similar usage in π., V. MM, VGT, see word). Pass.: [[r:1CO.14.38|1Co 14:38]], [[r:2CO.6.9|2Co 6:9]], [[r:GAL.1.22|Gal 1:22]].
(ἀγνοέω), a sin of ignorance (so in π.; see MM, VGT, see word): [[r:HEB.9.7|Heb 9:7.]]† (AS)
(ἀγνοέω), ignorance: [[r:ACT.3.17|Act 3:17 17:30]], [[r:EPH.4.18|Eph 4:18]] (with sense of wilful blindness; cf. MM, VGT, see word), [[r:1PE.1.14|1Pe 1:14.]]† (AS)

G0053.strongs: properly, clean, i.e. (figuratively) innocent, modest, perfect
senses: free from ceremonial defilement, in a condition prepared for worship (for exx. of pagan usage, V. MM, VGT, see word).

of things: [[r:PHP.4.8|Php 4:8]], [[r:JAS.3.17|Jas 3:17]], [[r:1PE.3.2|1Pe 3:2]]. † SYN.: εἰλικρινής (which see), pure, primarily as winnowed, purged, first found in ethical sense in NT (sincere). On the equivalence of ἁ. and καθαρός (which see), see DCG, ii, 459a though Westc. (Epp. Jo., 101) notes a distinction between them. (AS)
(γινώσκω), ignorance (opposite to γνῶσις): [[r:1CO.15.34|1Co 15:34]], [[r:1PE.2.15|1Pe 2:15]] (see Hort in l.; MM, VGT, see word).† (AS)

G0058.strongs: probably akin to); properly, the town-square (as a place of public resort); by implication, a market or thoroughfare
senses: a place of assembly, a public place or forum, a market-place (Hom., Thuc, al.; LXX): [[r:MAT.11.16|Mat 11:16 20:2 23:7]], [[r:MRK.6.56|Mrk 6:56]] (cf. MM, VGT, see word, ἀγυιά) 7:4 (Bl., §46, 7) 12:38, [[r:LUK.7.32|Luk 7:32]] (Bl., l.with) 11:43 20:46, [[r:ACT.16.19|Act 16:19 17:7]] (Cremer, 59; MM, VGT, see word). † (AS)

G0059.strongs: properly, to go to market, i.e. (by implication) to purchase; specially, to redeem
senses: to buy in the market, purchase (Xen., al.; LXX; in π. very common in deeds of sale, see MM, VGT, see word): absol., [[r:MAT.21.12|Mat 21:12]], [[r:MRK.11.15|Mrk 11:15]]; with accusative of thing(s), [[r:MAT.13.44|Mat 13:44, 46]], al.; before παρά, with genitive of person(s), [[r:REV.3.18|Rev 3:18]] (LXX, Polyb.); ἐκ, [[r:MAT.27.7|Mat 27:7]]; with genitive pret., [[r:MRK.6.37|Mrk 6:37]], al.; metaphorically, [[r:1CO.6.20|1Co 6:20 7:23]], [[r:2PE.2.1|2Pe 2:1]], [[r:REV.5.9|Rev 5:9 14:3, 4]]. (AS)

G0060.strongs: relating to the market-place, i.e. forensic (times); by implication, vulgar
senses: frequenting the ἀγορά , a lounger in the ἀγορά (Xen., al.): [[r:ACT.17.5|Act 17:5.]]

In late writers (Strab., al.), proper to the ἀγορά : ἀγοραῖοι (sc. ἥμεραι) ἀγονται (cf. Lat. conventus agere), court-days are kept, [[r:ACT.19.38|Act 19:38]] (for exx. of both usages, see MM, VGT, see word). † (AS)

G0061.strongs: (abstractly) a catching (of fish); also (concretely) a haul (of fish)
senses: that which is taken, a catch: of fish, [[r:LUK.5.9|Luk 5:9.]] † (AS)
ἀγραυλέω, -ῶ (ἀγραυλος, dwelling in the field; ἀγρός, αὐλή), to live in the fields: [[r:LUK.2.8|Luk 2:8.]]† (AS)
to catch or take by hunting or fishing; metaphorically, [[r:MRK.12.13|Mrk 12:13.]]† (AS)
As subst., the wild olive: [[r:ROM.11.17|Rom 11:17, 24]] (CGT, in 1.; MM, VGT, see word). † (AS)

G0066.strongs: wild (as pertaining to the country), literally (natural) or figuratively (fierce)
senses: savage, fierce: Ju 13. (Cf. usage in π. of a malignant wound; MM, VGT, see word) † (AS)

G0067.strongs: wild-horse tamer; Agrippas, one of the Herods

G0068.strongs: a field (as a drive for cattle); genitive case, the country; specially, a farm, i.e. hamlet
G0068.kjv: country, farm, piece of ground, land
senses: = χωρίον a piece of ground: [[r:MRK.10.29|Mrk 10:29]], [[r:ACT.4.27|Act 4:27]], al. (On the occurrence of this word as compared with χώρα, χωρίον see MM, VGT, see word) (AS)

G0069.strongs: to be sleepless, i.e. keep awake
senses: to be sleepless, wakeful (Theogn., Xen., al.); metaphorically (LXX) = cl. ἐγρήγορα, to be watchful, vigilant: [[r:MRK.13.33|Mrk 13:33]], [[r:LUK.21.36|Luk 21:36]], [[r:EPH.6.18|Eph 6:18]], [[r:HEB.13.17|Heb 13:17]].† SYN.: γρηγορέω, which see; νήφω, associated with γ. in [[r:1PE.5.8|1Pe 5:8]], expressing a wariness which results from self-control, a condition of moral, not merely mental alertness (see M, Th., I, 5:6). (AS)
sleeplessness, watching: [[r:2CO.6.5|2Co 6:5 11:27]]. (Plat., Hdt.; for exx. in π., see MM, VGT, see word) † (AS)

G0071.strongs: properly, to lead; by implication, to bring, drive, (reflexively) go, (specially) pass (time), or (figuratively) induce
G0071.kjv: be, bring (forth), carry, (let) go, keep, lead away, be open
senses: to lead, bring, carry: with ace, before ἐπί, εἰς, ἕως, πρός and simple dative; metaphorically, to lead, guide, impel: [[r:JHN.10.16|Jhn 10:16]] [[r:ROM.2.4|Rom 2:4]], [[r:HEB.2.10|Heb 2:10]], [[r:2TI.3.6|2Ti 3:6]], al.
Intrans., to go: subjunc., ἄγωμεν, [[r:MAT.2.46|Mat 2:46]], al. (Cramer, 61; MM, VGT, see word). (AS)

G0072.strongs: a bringing up, i.e. mode of living
senses: a leading, guiding; metaphorically, training; hence, from the expression ἀ. τοῦ βίου, absol., conduct, way of life: [[r:2TI.3.10|2Ti 3:10]] (Cremer, 61; MM, VGT, see word). † (AS)

G0073.strongs: properly, a place of assembly (as if led), i.e. (by implication) a contest (held there); figuratively, an effort or anxiety
senses: a contest, struggle, trial; metaphorically (MM, VGT, see word),
of the Christian life as a contest and struggle: [[r:PHP.1.30|Php 1:30]], [[r:1TH.2.2|1Th 2:2]], [[r:1TI.6.12|1Ti 6:12]], [[r:2TI.4.7|2Ti 4:7]] [[r:HEB.12.1|Heb 12:1]];

G0074.strongs: a struggle (properly, the state), i.e. (figuratively) anguish
senses: Of the mind, great fear, agony, anguish (Dem., Arist.): [[r:LUK.22.44|Luk 22:44]] (cf. Field, Notes, 77 f.; Abbott, Essays, 101 f.; MM, VGT, see word). † (AS)

G0075.strongs: to struggle, literally (to compete for a prize), figuratively (to contend with an adversary), or genitive case (to endeavor to accomplish something)
senses: to fight, struggle, strive: [[r:JHN.18.36|Jhn 18:36]]; metaphorically (MM, VGT, see word). [[r:COL.1.29|Col 1:29 4:12]], [[r:1TI.4.10|1Ti 4:10 6:12]], [[r:2TI.4.7|2Ti 4:7]]; with inf. (Field, Notes, 66), [[r:LUK.13.24|Luk 13:24]] (Cremer, 609) † (AS)

G0076.strongs: Adam, the first man; typically (of Jesus) man (as his representative)

senses: (ἀδελφός), a sister: [[r:MAT.19.29|Mat 19:29]], al.; metaphorically (MM, VGT, see word), of a member of the Christian community: [[r:ROM.16.1|Rom 16:1]], [[r:1CO.7.15|1Co 7:15]] [[r:JAS.21.15|Jas 21:15]], al. (AS)

G0080.root: from [[w:G0001]] (as a connective particle) and δελφύς (the womb)
G0080.strongs: a brother (literally or figuratively) near or remote (much like)
senses: (ἀ- copul., δελφύς, womb), in cl., a brother, born of the same parent or parents.

Of a member of the same nation ([[r:EXO.2.14|Exo 2:14]], [[r:DEU.15.3|Deu 15:3]]). In NT in each of these senses (1. [[r:MAT.1.2|Mat 1:2]], al.; 2. [[r:MAT.7.3|Mat 7:3]]; 3. [[r:ROM.9.3|Rom 9:3]]) and also,

of a fellow-Christian: [[r:1CO.1.1|1Co 1:1]], [[r:ACT.9.30|Act 9:30]]. This usage finds illustration in π., where ἀ. is used of members of a pagan religious community (M, Th., I, 1:4; MM, VGT, see word). The ἀδελφοὶ τ. Κυρίου ([[r:MAT.12.46|Mat 12:46-49 13:55 28:10]], [[r:MRK.3.31|Mrk 3:31-34]], [[r:LUK.8.19|Luk 8:19-21]], [[r:JHN.2.12|Jhn 2:12 7:3, 5 10 20:17]], [[r:ACT.1.14|Act 1:14]], [[r:1CO.9.5|1Co 9:5]]) may have been sons of Joseph and Mary (Mayor, Ja., Intr. viff.; DB, i, 320ff.) or of Joseph by a former marriage (Lft., Gal., 252ff.; DCG, i, 232ff.), but the view of Jerome, which makes ἀ. equivalent to ἀνεψιός, is inconsistent with Greek usage. (Cremer, 66.) (AS)

G0081.strongs: brotherhood (properly, the feeling of brotherliness), i.e. the (Christian) fraternity
senses: Concrete, the brotherhood, the Christian community: [[r:1PE.2.17|1Pe 2:17 5:9]] (MM, VGT, see word). † (AS)

G0085.forms: ἀδημονέω, -ῶ (on the derivation, see MM, VGT, see word)
G0085.root: from a derivative of ἀδέω (to be sated to loathing)
G0085.kjv: be full of heaviness, be very heavy

G0086.strongs: properly, unseen, i.e. "Hades" or the place (state) of departed souls
senses: in Hom., Hades (Pluto), the god of the underworld.

the abode of Hades, the underivorld; in NT, the abode of departed spirits, Hades: ἐν τ. ᾅ., [[r:LUK.16.23|Luk 16:23]]; εἰς ᾅ., [[r:ACT.2.27|Act 2:27,31]]; πύλαι ᾅδου, [[r:MAT.16.18|Mat 16:18]]; κλεῖς τοῦ ᾅ., [[r:REV.1.18|Rev 1:18]]; metaphorically, ἕως ᾅ., [[r:MAT.11.23|Mat 11:23]], [[r:LUK.10.15|Luk 10:15]]; personified, [[r:REV.6.8|Rev 6:8 20:13,14]] (Cremer, 67, 610; MM, VGT, see word). † (AS)

G0087.root: from [[w:G0001]] (as a negative particle) and a derivative of [[w:G1252]]
senses: not to be parted, mixed, undistinguishable (cf. Pr, l.with, and see Lft., Ignat. Eph., §3).
without uncertainty (Hort, in l., but see MM, VGT, see word): [[r:JAS.3.17|Jas 3:17.]] † (AS)

G0088.root: from [[w:G0001]] (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a compound of [[w:G1223]] and [[w:G3007]]
senses: (διαλείπω), unremitting, incessant: [[r:ROM.9.2|Rom 9:2]], [[r:2TI.1.3|2Ti 1:3]]. (For exx., see MM, VGT, see word) † (AS)

G0089.strongs: uninterruptedly, i.e. without omission (on an appropriate occasion)

G0091.strongs: to be unjust, i.e. (actively) do wrong (morally, socially or physically)
G0091.kjv: hurt, injure, be an offender, be unjust, (do, suffer, take) wrong
senses: intrans., to be ἄδικος, do wrong, act wickedly or criminally: [[r:ACT.25.11|Act 25:11]], [[r:1CO.6.8|1Co 6:8]], [[r:2CO.7.12|2Co 7:12]], [[r:COL.3.25|Col 3:25]], [[r:REV.22.11|Rev 22:11]]; to do hurt, [[r:REV.9.19|Rev 9:19.]]

to do some wrong: ὃ ἠδίκησεν, [[r:COL.3.25|Col 3:25]]; to wrong some one, [[r:MAT.20.13|Mat 20:13]], [[r:ACT.7.26|Act 7:26, 27 25:10]], [[r:2CO.7.2|2Co 7:2]], [[r:GAL.4.12|Gal 4:12]], Phm 18, [[r:2PE.2.13|2Pe 2:13]]; pass., [[r:ACT.7.24|Act 7:24]], [[r:2CO.7.12|2Co 7:12]]; mid., [[r:1CO.6.7|1Co 6:7]] (suffer... to be wronged; WM, §38, 3; but see Bl., §54, 5; and cf. ἀποστερέω);

G0092.kjv: evil doing, iniquity, matter of wrong

G0093.strongs: (legal) injustice (properly, the quality, by implication, the act); morally, wrongfulness (of character, life or act)
senses: unrighteousness, iniquity: [[r:JHN.7.18|Jhn 7:18]], [[r:ACT.8.23|Act 8:23]], [[r:ROM.1.18|Rom 1:18, 29 2:8 6:13]], [[r:2TI.2.19|2Ti 2:19]], [[r:1JN.1.9|1Jn 1:9 5:17]]; opposite to ἀλήθεια, [[r:1CO.13.6|1Co 13:6]], [[r:2TH.2.12|2Th 2:12]]; to δικαιοσύνη ], [[r:ROM.3.5|Rom 3:5]]; ἀπάτη τῆς ἀ., [[r:2TH.2.10|2Th 2:10]]; μισθὸς ἀδικίας, [[r:ACT.1.18|Act 1:18]], [[r:2PE.2.13|2Pe 2:13,15]]; ἐγράται τῆς ἀ., [[r:LUK.13.27|Luk 13:27]]; μαμωνᾶς τῆς ἀ., [[r:LUK.16.9|Luk 16:9]]; κόσμος τῆς ἀ., [[r:JAS.3.6|Jas 3:6]]; οἰκονόμος τῆς ἀ., [[r:LUK.16.8|Luk 16:8.]]
= ἀδίκημα, an unrighteous act: ironically, a favour, [[r:2CO.12.13|2Co 12:13]]; pl., [[r:HEB.8.12|Heb 8:12]] (Cremer, 261; MM, VGT, see word). † (AS)

G0094.strongs: unjust; by extension wicked; by implication, treacherous; specially, heathen
senses: unrighteous, wicked: [[r:LUK.16.11|Luk 16:11 18:11]], [[r:ACT.24.15|Act 24:15]], [[r:1CO.6.1|1Co 6:1]],9 [[r:1PE.3.18|1Pe 3:18]]; opposite to δίκαιος, [[r:MAT.5.45|Mat 5:45]]; to εὐσεβής, [[r:2PE.2.9|2Pe 2:9]]; to πιστός, [[r:LUK.16.10|Luk 16:10]] (Cremer, 200). † (AS)

G0096.strongs: unapproved, i.e. rejected; by implication, worthless (literally or morally)
senses: of things (prop. of metals: LXX, ll. with), not standing the test, rejected: γῆ, [[r:HEB.6.8|Heb 6:8.]]

Of liquids (Æsch., Eur., and late prose writers), genuine, pure (in π. and in MGr. of wine, also of corn: MM, VGT, see word; Milligan, NTD, 77): of milk, metaphorically, [[r:1PE.2.2|1Pe 2:2.]] † SYN.: ἀκέραιος (which see), ἄκακος, ἁπλοῦς. (AS)

G0098.root: from Ἀδραμύττειον (a place in Asia Minor)
senses: Ἁδραμυντηνός (T, Rec. Ἀδραμυττηνός), -ή,-όν, of Adramyttium, a seaport of Mysia: [[r:ACT.27.2|Act 27:2.]]† (AS)

G0099.root: from Ἀδρία (a place near its shore)
senses: Ἁδρίας (T, Rec. Ἀδρίας), -ου, ὁ, the Adriatic sea, in later Greek usage extended to take in all the waters between Greece and Italy: [[r:ACT.27.27|Act 27:27.]]† (AS)
come! used as adv. and addressed, like φέρε, to one or more persons: [[r:JAS.4.13|Jas 4:13, 5:1]].† (AS)

ἅγιος, -α, ον (τό ἅγός, religious awe; ἅζω, to venerate), primarily, dedicated to the gods, sacred (Hdt.; rare in Att., never in Hom., Hes. and Trag., who use ἁγνός), hence, holy, characteristic of God, separated to God, worthy of veneration.
Its highest application is to God himself, in his purity, majesty, and glory: [[r:LUK.1.49|Luk 1:49]], [[r:JHN.17.11|Jhn 17:11]], [[r:REV.4.8|Rev 4:8]]. Hence
of things and places which have a claim to reverence as sacred to God, e.g. the Temple: [[r:MAT.24.15|Mat 24:15]], [[r:HEB.9.1|Heb 9:1]];
of persons employed by him, as angels: [[r:1TH.3.13|1Th 3:13]]; prophets, [[r:LUK.1.70|Luk 1:70]]; apostles, [[r:EPH.3.5|Eph 3:5.]]
Applied to persons as separated to God's service:
In the moral sense of sharing God's purity: [[r:MRK.6.20|Mrk 6:20]], [[r:JHN.17.11|Jhn 17:11]], [[r:ACT.3.14|Act 3:14]], [[r:REV.3.7|Rev 3:7]].

Of pure, clean sacrifices and offerings: [[r:1CO.7.14|1Co 7:14]], [[r:EPH.1.4|Eph 1:4]]. SYN.: ἁγνός, pure, both in ceremonial and spiritual sense; ἱερός (sacer), sacred, that which is inviolable because of its (external) relation to God; ὅσιος (sanctus as opposite to nefas), that which is based on everlasting ordinances of right. (Cf. Tr., Syn., §lxxxviii; DB, ii, 399 f.; Cremer, 34, 594-601; MM, VGT, see word) (AS)

G0090.root: from a derivative of a compound of [[w:G0001]] (as a negative particle) and a derivative of [[w:G1311]]
